0.long_answer: Fibular aplasia-ectrodactyly syndrome is a very rare genetic condition that is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner with incomplete penetrance. It is characterized by the absence (aplasia) or underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the fibula combined with limb malformations such as split-hand/foot malformation, which may include shortened digits (brachydactyly) or fusion of digits (syndactyly). The syndrome may also be accompanied by defects in the femur, tibia, or other joint anomalies, and further highlights the variability in clinical presentation despite its specific genetic etiology.
